transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date/Time: 2025-08-19 15:30 UTC
Duration: ~46 minutes
Attendees: Ethan (Redwood AE), Sofia (Redwood SE), Leah (Redwood CSM); Asha (FinSecure CISO), Mark (FinSecure Head of Platform), Jonas (SRE), Priya (Legal)

Summary:
High-level security review focused on encryption at rest/in transit, key management (KMS, BYOK, HSM), key rotation, and audit logging. Customer wants to understand Redwood's options for customer-managed keys, hardware security modules, and how audit logs and RBAC integrate into their compliance requirements (SOC 2 / ISO).

Topics Covered:
- Encryption at rest architecture, envelope encryption, CMKs vs DEKs
- BYOK flows and HSM integration options (cloud HSM vs on-prem HSM)
- How Redwood Private / Dedicated handle keys and network isolation
- Audit logs, key rotation, and access controls (SSO/SAML, RBAC)
- Data residency and contractual obligations

Transcript:
[00:00] Ethan (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intros?
[00:08] Asha (FinSecure): Asha Patel, CISO. We'll mostly be focused on encryption, key ownership and audit requirements, and Lea, Priya and Mark are on for questions.
[00:18] Mark (FinSecure): Mark Liu, I run platform. We're evaluating Redwood Private for some customer PII workloads.
[00:25] Sofia (Redwood SE): Great - I'll cover the technical flows for BYOK and HSM options after Ethan gives the compliance overview.
[00:32] Ethan: High level - Redwood supports encryption in transit via TLS 1.2+ and TLS 1.3, and encryption at rest. For managed hosted API keys we control the CMKs, but for enterprise we support BYOK with cloud KMS and HSM-backed keys.
[00:50] Jonas (SRE): Can you clarify what BYOK means in practice? Are we handing you keys or do we keep the master in our HSM?
[00:59] Sofia: Two modes: 1) Cloud BYOK - you provision a customer-managed CMK in your cloud KMS (AWS KMS/GCP KMS/Azure) and we reference it for envelope encryption; Redwood never persists the plaintext master. 2) HSM bring-your-own - with Private, you can deploy an HSM (cloud HSM or on-prem HSM) and we integrate via standard PKCS#11 or Cloud HSM APIs. There's a flow diagram I can share.
[01:25] Asha: And how are keys rotated? Automatic rotation? Manual? Tell me about key material lifecycle.
[01:32] Sofia: We support rotation policies. For cloud KMS, rotation can be managed by your KMS (we use the active key version for envelope wrapping). For HSM, rotation is coordinate with your ops team - Redwood will request new wrapping key IDs and we will switch to new CMK versions with a safe rollout. We keep wrapped data encryption keys (DEKs) only, not plaintext CMKs.
[01:58] Mark: Do we need network peering for private key calls or is it over mutual TLS to the KMS endpoint?
[02:04] Sofia: For cloud KMS we call the KMS endpoints over TLS; for dedicated Private with VPC, we recommend VPC peering or PrivateLink to reduce exposure and satisfy egress controls.
[02:15] Priya (Legal): Contractually we need to ensure key escrow options are documented, and we need indemnities around key misuse. Is there a standard addendum?
[02:23] Ethan: We have a security addendum template for BYOK customers that covers responsibilities and key handling. I'll send the latest version.
[02:30] Jonas: What about HSM providers? We currently use an on-prem Thales-like device - can Redwood integrate?
[02:36] Sofia: Yes - we support PKCS#11 and common HSM middleware. For on-prem HSMs, we recommend running a Redwood Private control plane inside the same network to avoid egress of unwrapped keys. The model is envelope encryption: DEKs are encrypted with your CMK in the HSM, Redwood stores only those wrapped DEKs.
[02:58] Asha: Is the audit logging for key accesses available? We need detailed logs for every decryption/call referencing key usage.
[03:05] Sofia: We log key operation references as part of request traces in Redwood Console. For cloud KMS, the KMS provider (AWS CloudTrail, GCP Audit Logs) will have the cryptographic operations too. We can stream audit logs to your SIEM - we support pushing logs to S3/GCS or to syslog endpoints.
[03:25] Mark: Any potential performance hit? We need sub-200ms 95p for low latency routes. Wrapping/unwrapping on each request sounds expensive.
[03:34] Sofia: We use envelope encryption with caching of DEKs and a KV cache - so unwrap operations are infrequent. Only key operations happen on key rotation or cache miss. There may be a small cold-start overhead. Note: sometimes transcripts show KV "cash" in our docs, that's just a transcription glitch.
[03:55] Ethan: Also mention that Redwood Dedicated can be configured with local key caching and local HSM in the same rack for minimal latency.
[04:05] Asha: For SOC 2, we need proof on how keys are protected and on separation of duties. Do you have an SOC 2 report with KMS practices?
[04:12] Ethan: Yes - SOC 2 Type II covers our control environment; for BYOK customers we provide a supplemental note showing how CMKs are not accessible to Redwood operators. I'll attach the report.
[04:23] Priya: We need to confirm which Redwood roles can request key unwraps or rotate keys - RBAC detail.
[04:30] Sofia: RBAC is configurable in the Console. We map SAML groups to roles; you can restrict key admin to specific groups. Audit logs capture admin actions (key rotate requests, key attachments).
[04:45] Jonas: On the private deployment, what about HSM firmware updates - would Redwood manage that?
[04:50] Sofia: Typically the customer manages on-prem HSM firmware; for cloud HSM we coordinate maintenance windows. We document responsibilities in the runbook.
[05:00] Asha: If we do BYOK with AWS KMS, are there any metadata leaks we should be aware of - like key IDs in logs?
[05:08] Sofia: Key IDs may appear in audit logs; we can anonymize or truncate certain fields in our log stream if required. We'll discuss retention and PIIs in logs.
[05:20] Ethan: Data residency - you mentioned EU and US regions?
[05:24] Mark: Primary processing in eu-west-1, backups in us-east-1 is a hard constraint for some datasets.
[05:30] Sofia: Redwood Private can be deployed into specific regions and you can pin models and storage to those regions. For hosted, we have region controls as well, but for stricter residency we recommend Private.
[05:42] Asha: Encryption in transit - any TLS termination in public layer? We need end-to-end encryption to our VPC.
[05:49] Sofia: For Private and Dedicated you can enforce mutual TLS and VPC-level controls; for hosted we terminate TLS at our edge but connections to downstream backends use TLS and we support mTLS for integrations.
[05:59] Jonas: What about key compromise response - do you have a rotation and rewrap plan that avoids data loss?
[06:05] Sofia: Yes - we support rewrapping DEKs with a new CMK version. We have procedures for emergency rotation and can run a bulk rewrap job. We'll include runbook excerpts in the follow-up docs.
[06:20] Priya: Are there certifications for HSMs - do you support FIPS 140-2/3 validated modules?
[06:26] Sofia: We integrate with FIPS-validated cloud HSMs (AWS CloudHSM) and support customer-provided FIPS devices. We'll note which modules are validated in the options doc.
[06:38] Mark: Any limitations around model caching and data leakage? We need to ensure prompt and outputs for PII are not cached inadvertently.
[06:46] Ethan: We have options to disable persistent prompt caching and enforce strict retention policies; Redwood Optimize suggestions won't run if you have retention disabled.
[06:57] Asha: How granular are logs for function/tool calls and who invoked them? We need a chain-of-custody for each inference that touches sensitive data.
[07:05] Sofia: We log request-id, user/service identity (via API key or SSO user), route/model used, tokens, and the decision points (fallbacks, rollouts). We redact sensitive content in logs and can provide hashed references for chain-of-custody.
[07:24] Ethan: Quick note on HSM key storage patterns - we recommend envelope encryption where DEKs are rotated frequently and CMKs are used sparingly to limit HSM ops.
[07:35] Mark: Ok makes sense. For cost, how expensive is HSM usage?
[07:40] Sofia: HSM ops on cloud HSMs are billed separately (per-hour cluster + per-op in some providers). We'll include a rough TCO estimate in the options doc.
[07:50] Asha: Anything about multi-tenant isolation? We need guarantees that other tenants can't see our key IDs or wrapped DEKs.
[07:57] Sofia: In Dedicated and Private, there is tenant isolation at multiple layers; we also separate metadata and encrypt storage namespaces. We'll document separation controls.
[08:10] Jonas: Is there an emergency kill-switch if a key is compromised? We need ability to disable a model route quickly.
[08:16] Ethan: Yes - console allows disabling routes, and policy-based fallback can route to a lower-sensitivity model. We'll show examples.
[08:26] Priya: For contract, can we add clauses around breach notification timelines and key compromise SLA?
[08:31] Ethan: That's negotiable; our legal team has standard language. I'll loop in legal after this call.
[08:38] Asha: Regarding audit logs retention, we need 7 years for certain data; can you store that?
[08:44] Sofia: We can stream logs to your archival storage with lifecycle policies. Long retention increases cost; we'll provide options.
[08:55] Mark: Anything else around SSO - we use SAML and SCIM provisioning.
[09:00] Sofia: We support SAML 2.0 SSO and SCIM for provisioning and group sync. RBAC mapping supports fine-grained roles mapped from SAML attributes.
[09:12] Ethan: Ok, recap of immediate deliverables on our side and next steps.
[09:16] (discussion continues - omitted repetitive portions)
[30:00] Sofia: --- jumping ahead, example BYOK flow: customer creates CMK in AWS KMS -> Redwood requests IAM role to call kms:Encrypt/wrapKey only -> we store wrapped DEKs -> runtime unwrap uses KMS only on cache miss -> DEKs cached in memory and rotated per policy.
[31:10] Asha: For legal we need a diagram and precise list of API calls made to KMS for audit.
[31:20] Ethan: We'll include the API call list and CloudTrail event IDs.
[32:00] Jonas: Any support for HSM-backed key attestation? We want attestations for key origin.
[32:08] Sofia: Yes - attestation tokens from some HSMs are supported; we'll include attestation workflow where available.
[33:30] Mark: Final question - is Redwood staff ever able to decrypt customer data when BYOK is used?
[33:38] Sofia: Not when BYOK with customer-managed CMKs is in place - Redwood operators do not have access to CMK plaintext. Access to decrypt content requires the customer-managed key to perform wrap/unwrap; we can add additional logging to demonstrate separation.
[34:05] Ethan: Great - let's confirm the follow-ups. I'll send the SOC2 and security addendum; Sofia will send the BYOK/HSM options doc and TCO; we'll schedule the infra deep-dive next week.
[34:25] Asha: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.

Recap / Next steps (verbal):
- Ethan to share SOC 2 Type II, security addendum, and network diagram
- Sofia to prepare BYOK/HSM integration options, attestation details, and cost estimates
- Schedule a technical deep dive with FinSecure infra team (aim week of Aug 25)
